questions.explanation: A coat goes on the upper body, so it takes きる (group 2): きて + います = きています.

questions.stem: {今|いま}、{何|なに}をしていますか。 Which is the best answer?
choices: {本|ほん}を{読|よ}んでください。
questions.explanation: The question asks what you are doing now, so answer with the action in progress: {読|よ}んでいます. {読|よ}みます is for habits and the future ("I read" / "I will read"), not "I'm reading".

questions.stem: What does {父|ちち}は{今|いま}アメリカへ{行|い}っています mean?
choices: My father will go to America.
My father is on his way to America now.
My father is in America now (he went there).
My father goes to America often.
questions.explanation: With {行|い}く, 〜ています is the result: he has gone and is there now. It never means "on his way"; for that, Japanese uses other words.

questions.stem: Choose the particle: おおさか___すんでいます。
questions.explanation: すむ takes に for the place you live: おおさかにすんでいます. で marks where an action happens and sounds wrong here, a common mistake from English "in".

questions.stem: How is the sign 入口 read?
questions.explanation: 入口 is いりぐち, entrance. 入 uses the reading い(る) here, and 口 (mouth, opening) softens to ぐち. The exit, 出口, is でぐち.

questions.stem: How is the verb read? {母|はは}は{今|いま}出かけています。
questions.explanation: 出かける is でかける, to go out: {母|はは}は{今|いま}{出|で}かけています, my mother is out. 出 is read だ only in {出|だ}す (to take out); シュツ is an on reading used in compounds.

questions.stem: What does the kanji 立 mean?
questions.explanation: 立 is stand: {立|た}つ, to stand. Enter is 入, go out is 出, and sit (すわる) isn't written with a course kanji.

questions.stem: Listen. What is the person doing?

audio.text: めがねをかけています

questions.explanation: めがねをかけています: (she) has her glasses on. Taking them off would be めがねをとっています or めがねをとりました.

questions.stem: Listen. Which sentence did you hear?

audio.text: しろいシャツをきています

choices: {白|しろ}いシャツをきています。
{白|しろ}いシャツをきってください。
{白|しろ}いシャツをきたいです。
{白|しろ}いシャツをきました。
questions.explanation: "Kite imasu" with no small っ: きています, is wearing. きって would be the て form of きる "to cut".

questions.stem: Listen and type what you hear, in hiragana: ___

audio.text: しっています

questions.explanation: "Shitte imasu", I know: しっています. しる is group 1, so the て form is しって, with a small っ.

questions.stem: Choose the right form: パンを___います (I'm cutting the bread).
questions.explanation: きる "to cut" is group 1 (きります), so る → って: きって. きて is the て form of the other きる, "to wear" (group 2).

questions.stem: Which verb fits? コーヒーにミルクを___ます。 (I put milk in my coffee.)
questions.explanation: Putting something in is {入|い}れる (group 2, takes を): {入|い}れます. {入|はい}ります is for going in yourself (へやに{入|はい}ります), and {出|だ}します is taking out.

questions.stem:
Read the text. Which statement is true?
あにはカナダにすんでいます。{会社|かいしゃ}につとめています。けっこんしていません。
choices: He is moving to Canada next year.
He is visiting Canada on business.
He works for a company in Canada and is single.
He is married and lives in Canada.
questions.explanation: すんでいます: he lives there; {会社|かいしゃ}につとめています: he works for a company; けっこんしていません: he isn't married. None of the ている forms here describe something happening right now.

questions.stem: Match each item to the verb for wearing it.
questions.explanation: きる for the top half, はく for legs and feet, かぶる for the head, かける for glasses, する for ties and watches. ぬぐ is taking clothes off.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "My mother is out right now"?
choices: {母|はは}は{今|いま}{出|で}かけました。
{母|はは}は{今|いま}{出|で}かけています。
{母|はは}は{今|いま}{出|で}かけます。
{母|はは}は{今|いま}{出|で}かけてください。
questions.explanation: {出|で}かける happens in a moment; 〜ています gives the result, "she has gone out and is out". {出|で}かけます is "she's about to go out" and {出|で}かけました only says she left.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I got up, had breakfast and went to school"?
choices: おきて、あさごはんを{食|た}べて、{学校|がっこう}へ{行|い}きました。
おきて、あさごはんを{食|た}べました、{学校|がっこう}へ{行|い}って。
おきる、あさごはんを{食|た}べる、{学校|がっこう}へ{行|い}きました。
おきました、あさごはんを{食|た}べました、{学校|がっこう}へ{行|い}きました。
questions.explanation: Every verb but the last is in the て form, and the last one ({行|い}きました) carries the past tense for the whole chain. Putting ました on each verb strings three sentences together.

questions.stem: Choose the form: しゅくだいを___から、テレビを{見|み}ます。
questions.explanation: 〜てから (after doing) always follows the て form: してから. するから or しますから would be "because I do", the から of reasons, which is a different pattern.

questions.stem: Choose the particle: じゅぎょう___まえに、{先生|せんせい}にしつもんしました。
questions.explanation: After a noun, まえに needs の: じゅぎょうのまえに, before class. Leaving it out (じゅぎょうまえに) is a common mistake.

questions.stem: Choose the form: ___まえに、はをみがきます。 (before going to bed)
questions.explanation: Before まえに a verb is in the dictionary form: ねるまえに. The ます form and the て form don't go here, and の is only for nouns.

questions.stem: Type the missing word (after class I go to the library): じゅぎょうの___で、としょかんへ{行|い}きます。
questions.explanation: N のあとで is "after N": じゅぎょうのあとで. まえ would be "before".

questions.stem: What does {日本|にほん}へ{来|き}てから、{日本語|にほんご}をべんきょうしています mean?
choices: I came to Japan to study Japanese.
I studied Japanese before I came to Japan.
I'll study Japanese after I come to Japan.
I've been studying Japanese since I came to Japan.
questions.explanation: 〜てから + 〜ています means "since doing": the studying started when you came and is still going on. "Came to study" would be べんきょうしに{来|き}ました (lesson 20).

questions.stem: How is this word read? {来年|らいねん}、外国へ{行|い}きます。
questions.explanation: 外国 is がいこく, a foreign country. Both kanji use their on readings: ガイ and コク. 国 becomes ゴク only in some words, such as {中国|ちゅうごく}.

questions.stem: How is this word read? いもうとは高校生です。
questions.explanation: 高校生 is こうこうせい, high school student: 高 (コウ, high) + 校 (コウ, school) + 生 (セイ). たか is the reading of 高 in {高|たか}い, not in this word.

questions.stem: What does the kanji 語 mean in {日本語|にほんご} and {外国語|がいこくご}?
questions.explanation: 語 (ゴ) means language or word. Country is 国, school 校, and person 人 ({日本人|にほんじん}).

questions.stem: Which kanji means "country" and is read くに on its own?
questions.explanation: 国 is country (くに; コク in {外国|がいこく}). 口 (mouth), 四 (four) and 日 (day) are also boxes, but only 国 has a jewel inside its border.

questions.stem: Type in Japanese: What language is this? (use これは): ___
questions.explanation: これは{何語|なにご}ですか. {何語|なにご} is read なにご, not なんご: 何 + 語, "what language".

questions.stem: Listen. When is the speaker going to the library?

audio.text: じゅぎょうのあとで、としょかんへ行きます

questions.explanation: じゅぎょうのあとで: after class. Before class would be じゅぎょうのまえに.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker do first?

audio.text: 手をあらってから、食べます

questions.explanation: {手|て}をあらってから、{食|た}べます: after washing my hands, I eat. The action in the てから part comes first.

questions.stem: Listen and type the word you hear, in hiragana: ___

audio.text: しゅくだい

questions.explanation: "Shukudai", homework: しゅくだい, with a small ゅ after し.

questions.stem: What is the polite way to ask someone where they are from?
choices: おくにはどちらですか。
わたしのおくにはどこですか。
おくにへ{行|い}きますか。
questions.explanation: おくにはどちらですか uses お for the other person's country and polite どちら for どこ. お is never used for your own country, and だれ means who.

questions.stem: Choose the verb: じゅぎょうは{九時|くじ}に___。
questions.explanation: Class begins by itself, so it's はじまる: じゅぎょうがはじまります. はじめる needs someone doing the starting and an object with を ({先生|せんせい}がじゅぎょうをはじめます).

questions.stem:
Read the text. What does Maria do before going to bed?
{毎日|まいにち}、じゅぎょうのあとで、としょかんでしゅくだいをします。ねるまえに、{新|あたら}しいことばを{十|とお}おぼえます。
choices: She does her homework in the library.
questions.explanation: ねるまえに (before going to bed) goes with {新|あたら}しいことばを{十|とお}おぼえます: she memorizes ten new words. The homework in the library is after class.

questions.stem: What does うちにかえって、ばんごはんを{食|た}べました mean?
choices: I had dinner and then went home.
I had dinner at home after I went out.
I went home and then had dinner.
I'll go home and have dinner.
questions.explanation: In a て chain the verbs come in the order the actions happened: first かえって (went home), then {食|た}べました (ate). The final ました makes it past, so it can't be "I'll go".

questions.stem: {本|ほん}を{読|よ}みました。___、ねました。 Which word fits?
questions.explanation: それから (and then, after that) starts a new sentence that follows on from the last one. まえに needs something before it, から can't start a sentence, and あとで on its own means "later" (I'll do it later), not "and then" after an action you've just named.

questions.stem: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explanation: {高校|こうこう} high school, {外国|がいこく} abroad, しゅくだい homework, じしょ dictionary, ことば word. A classroom is きょうしつ and a question しつもん.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "May I sit here?"
choices: ここにすわってはいけませんか。
ここにすわってください。
ここにすわってもいいですか。
questions.explanation: Asking permission is the て form + もいいですか: すわってもいいですか. すわってください asks someone else to sit, and すわりますか asks whether they will sit.

questions.stem: Choose the particle: ここでしゃしんをとって___いけません。
questions.explanation: Prohibition is 〜てはいけません, with は. も belongs to permission (〜てもいいです); mixing the two is the most common mistake with these patterns.

questions.stem: Choose the particle: まどをあけて___いいですか。
questions.explanation: Permission is 〜てもいいですか, with も: "even if I open it, is it all right?" は goes with いけません.

questions.stem: A guest in your home asks: たばこをすってもいいですか。 You'd rather they didn't. What is the polite answer?
choices: いいえ、すってはいけません。
questions.explanation: The polite no is すみません、ちょっと…, letting the sentence trail off. いいえ、すってはいけません is grammatical but sounds like a rule read out to a child. はい、どうぞ says yes.

questions.stem: A sign says: ここで{食|た}べてはいけません。 What does it mean?
questions.explanation: 〜てはいけません means "must not": you must not eat here. "You may eat here" would be {食|た}べてもいいです.

questions.stem: What does あたまがいたいです mean?
questions.explanation: あたま (head) + がいたい (hurts): a headache. "Clever" is あたまがいい; a stomachache is おなかがいたい.

questions.stem: Choose the verb: ごはんの{後|あと}で、このくすりを___ください。
questions.explanation: Japanese "drinks" medicine, even pills: くすりを{飲|の}む. くすりを{食|た}べる is the English-speaker's mistake.

questions.stem: How is the kanji read? 目がいたいです。
questions.explanation: 目 on its own is め, eye: my eyes hurt. モク is its on reading, used in compounds. みみ is 耳 (ear) and くち is 口 (mouth).

questions.stem: What does the kanji 耳 mean?
questions.explanation: 耳 (みみ) is ear; it's also inside 聞 (listen). Eye is 目, mouth 口, hand 手.

questions.stem: Which kanji means "hand"?
questions.explanation: 手 (て) is hand. 千 (thousand), 子 (child) and 午 (noon) look a little alike, but only 手 has three crossing strokes like spread fingers.

questions.stem: How is the kanji read? たくさんあるいて、足がいたいです。
questions.explanation: 足 on its own is あし, foot or leg. ソク is the on reading, used in compounds; て is 手 (hand).

questions.stem: Listen. What hurts?

audio.text: のどがいたいです

questions.explanation: のどがいたいです: I have a sore throat. Ear is {耳|みみ}, stomach おなか, head あたま.

questions.stem: Listen. What happened to the speaker?

audio.text: かぜをひきました

questions.explanation: かぜをひきました: I've caught a cold. かぜ also means wind, but かぜをひく is always the cold. A fever is ねつ.

questions.stem: Listen and type what you hear, in hiragana: ___

audio.text: おだいじに

questions.explanation: "Odaiji ni", get well soon: おだいじに. You say it to someone who is ill.

questions.stem: Ask "May I go home?" using かえる (to go home): ___
accept: かえってもいいですか
かえってもいいですか？
questions.explanation: かえる is group 1, so its て form is かえって; add もいいですか: かえってもいいですか. かえてもいいですか uses the group 2 form by mistake.

questions.stem: Which word means "hospital"?
questions.explanation: びょういん, with a small ょ, is a hospital or clinic. びよういん, with a full-size よ and one more beat, is a hair salon. びょうき is illness; くすり medicine.

questions.stem:
Read the pool rules. Which is NOT allowed?
プールに{入|はい}るまえに、シャワーをあびてください。プールのまわりではしってはいけません。{水|みず}の{中|なか}で、ぼうしをかぶってください。
choices: Wearing a cap in the water
questions.explanation: はしってはいけません: you must not run. Showering first and wearing a cap are things you are asked to do (〜てください).

questions.stem: The doctor asks: どうしましたか。 Which is a natural answer?
questions.explanation: どうしましたか is "what's the matter?", so say what's wrong: おなかがいたいです. おだいじに is what the doctor says to you at the end.

questions.stem: Match each kanji to its meaning.
questions.explanation: 目 め eye, 耳 みみ ear, 口 くち mouth, 手 て hand, 足 あし foot or leg. Head (あたま) and tooth (は) aren't written with course kanji.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "You may speak English"?
choices: えいごで{話|はな}してはいけません。
えいごで{話|はな}してください。
えいごで{話|はな}してもいいです。
えいごで{話|はな}しています。
questions.explanation: 〜てもいいです is "you may". 〜てはいけません is the opposite, 〜てください is a request ("please speak"), and 〜ています describes someone speaking.

questions.stem: How do you say "want to eat" with {食|た}べる?
questions.explanation: たい goes on the ます stem: {食|た}べ-ます → {食|た}べたい. It never follows the dictionary form or the て form.

questions.stem: How do you say "I don't want to go"?
questions.explanation: たい changes like an い-adjective: い → くない, so {行|い}きたくないです. ません is for verbs and じゃない for nouns and な-adjectives.

questions.stem: Choose the particle: {新|あたら}しいカメラ___ほしいです。
questions.explanation: ほしい is an adjective, and the thing wanted takes が: カメラがほしいです. を is a common mistake carried over from the verb {買|か}う.

questions.stem: Choose the form: {本|ほん}を___に{行|い}きます。 (I'm going to buy a book.)
questions.explanation: Purpose uses the ます stem + に: {買|か}い-ます → {買|か}いに{行|い}きます. The dictionary form ({買|か}うに) and the て form don't go here.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I'm going shopping"?
questions.explanation: With a noun for an activity, purpose is N + に: {買|か}いものに{行|い}きます. で would be "by means of shopping", and を and が make no sense with {行|い}く here.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I want a new bag"?
choices: {新|あたら}しいかばんを{買|か}いほしいです。
{新|あたら}しいかばんがほしいたいです。
{新|あたら}しいかばんがたいです。
{新|あたら}しいかばんがほしいです。
questions.explanation: For a thing, use N がほしいです. たい only goes on verbs ({買|か}いたい), and ほしい never follows a verb stem.

questions.stem: How do you say "I wanted to see that film"?
choices: そのえいがを{見|み}ましたい。
そのえいがを{見|み}たかったです。
そのえいがを{見|み}たいでした。
そのえいがを{見|み}たくないです。
questions.explanation: The past of たい is like an い-adjective: い → かった, {見|み}たかったです. {見|み}たいでした is like saying たかいでした, wrong for い-adjectives. {見|み}たくないです means "don't want to".

questions.stem: You're planning a trip and want to know whether Emma would like to come. Which is most natural?
choices: エマさんはほしいですか。
エマさんも{行|い}きたいでしたか。
エマさんも{行|い}きたいですか。
エマさんは{行|い}きたいです。
questions.explanation: Japanese doesn't state another person's wishes (エマさんは{行|い}きたいです sounds wrong), but you can ask the person: エマさんも{行|い}きたいですか. ほしい is for things and needs one.

questions.stem: How is this word read? デパートへ買いものに{行|い}きます。
questions.explanation: 買いもの is かいもの, shopping. 買 uses its kun reading か(う); バイ is its on reading, used in other words. The い comes from the ます stem {買|か}い-ます.

questions.stem: What does the kanji 買 mean?
questions.explanation: 買 (か-う) means buy. Sell is うる (written in kana in this course), shop is 店 (みせ) and money is お{金|かね}.

questions.stem: In a shop, you've decided on a sweater. What do you say?
choices: じゃあ、これをさがしています。
じゃあ、これはありますか。
questions.explanation: 〜にします is how you choose: これにします, "I'll take this one". さがしています means you are still looking for something.

questions.stem: Listen. How does the speaker feel?

audio.text: おなかがすきました

questions.explanation: おなかがすきました: I'm hungry (literally "my stomach has become empty"). Thirsty is のどがかわきました; sleepy is ねむいです.

questions.stem: Listen. Why is the speaker going to the department store?

audio.text: デパートへくつを買いに行きます

questions.explanation: くつを{買|か}いに{行|い}きます: going to buy shoes. The ます stem + に gives the purpose.

questions.stem: Listen and type what you hear, in hiragana: ___

audio.text: ほしいです

questions.explanation: "Hoshii desu", I want (it): ほしいです.

questions.stem: Type the polite たい form of {飲|の}む: "want to drink" ___
questions.explanation: ます stem {飲|の}み + たい + です: {飲|の}みたいです. No sound change here: that is only for the て form.

questions.stem:
Read the text. Why did Ken buy a sweater?
{母|はは}のたんじょうびのプレゼントを{買|か}いたかったです。{母|はは}は「かばんがほしいです」と{言|い}っていました。でも、かばんは{高|たか}かったです。それで、セーターを{買|か}いました。
questions.explanation: でも、かばんは{高|たか}かったです: but the bags were expensive. それで (so) introduces the result: he bought a sweater instead.

questions.stem: How do you ask "Do you have it in another colour?"
choices: ほかのいろをさがしてください。
ほかのいろはありますか。
ほかのいろにしますか。
ほかのいろがほしいですか。
questions.explanation: ほかのいろはありますか: is there another colour? ほしいですか asks the shop assistant what they want, and 〜にしますか is what staff ask you.

questions.stem: Type the missing particle (I'm going for a walk): さんぽ___いきます。
questions.explanation: Purpose takes に: さんぽに{行|い}きます. へ marks a destination, and a walk isn't a place.

questions.stem: A shop assistant asks if you need help. You're looking for a black bag. What do you say?
choices: くろいかばんをさがしています。
くろいかばんをさがしたかったです。
くろいかばんをさがしてください。
くろいかばんがさがしています。
questions.explanation: さがしています (I'm looking for) is the action in progress. さがしてください asks the assistant to do the looking, which is a bit abrupt, and さがす takes を, not が.

questions.stem: Match each English meaning to the Japanese.
questions.explanation: たい changes like an い-adjective (たくない, たかった). Purpose uses the ます stem: {食|た}べに{行|い}く. {食|た}べたいない and {食|た}べるに{行|い}く are both wrong.

questions.stem: As you enter a restaurant, the staff call out いらっしゃいませ. How should you respond?
choices: Say いらっしゃいませ back.
Say ごちそうさまでした.
No answer is needed; a nod or smile is enough.
questions.explanation: いらっしゃいませ is a welcome, not a question, and customers don't answer it in words. Saying it back sounds as if you were the staff; いただきます is for the start of the meal and ごちそうさまでした for the end.

questions.stem: The waiter asks {何名|なんめい}さまですか。 You are two. What do you say?
questions.explanation: Customers use the ordinary people counter: {二人|ふたり}です. 〜{名|めい}さま is the staff's polite word for you, not one you use about yourself; 〜つ is for things and ふつか is the second of the month.

questions.stem: What is an おしぼり for?
questions.explanation: The おしぼり, a small wet towel, is for your hands. Using it on your face is common in casual places but best avoided in smart ones; it isn't for the table.

questions.stem: You're ready to order, but no one comes to your table. What do you do?
choices: Wait until a waiter comes to check on you.
Raise a hand slightly and call すみません！
questions.explanation: Waiters usually don't come by on their own; calling すみません！ is normal and polite. Some tables have a call button instead. Snapping your fingers is rude anywhere.

questions.stem: What is a ていしょく?
choices: A shared dish for the whole table
A set meal with rice, miso soup and side dishes
A drink included with every meal
questions.explanation: A ていしょく is a set meal: one main dish with rice, miso soup and small sides such as pickles. It's often the best value at lunch.

questions.stem: Which of these is bad manners at a Japanese table?
choices: Standing your chopsticks upright in your rice
Lifting your rice bowl to your mouth
Drinking miso soup from the bowl
questions.explanation: Chopsticks standing upright in rice recall a funeral offering, so avoid it. Lifting small bowls, drinking miso soup from the bowl and slurping noodles are all normal.

questions.stem: Ask for the bill: ___をおねがいします。
questions.explanation: おかいけいをおねがいします: the bill, please. Usually you then pay at the register (レジ) by the door.

questions.stem: How much should you tip in a Japanese restaurant?
choices: Leave your coins on the table.
questions.explanation: Japan has no tipping; service is included. If you leave money on the table, staff may chase after you to return it.

questions.stem: Listen. What is the customer asking?

audio.text: おすすめは何ですか

questions.explanation: おすすめは{何|なん}ですか: what do you recommend? "What is this?" would be これは{何|なん}ですか.

questions.stem: Listen. What did the waiter ask?

audio.text: なんめいさまですか

choices: What would you like to order?
How many people are in your party?
questions.explanation: {何名|なんめい}さまですか: how many of you are there? It uses the polite counter 〜{名|めい} for people. A reservation would be ごよやくは？

questions.stem:
Read the sign at a ramen shop. What should you do first?
しょっけんを{買|か}ってから、すわってください。
(しょっけん = meal ticket)
questions.explanation: 〜てから, then the next action: buy a meal ticket, then sit down. At ticket-machine shops you don't order from a person.

questions.stem: Order the curry by saying "I'll have the curry." (Type カレー in CAPITALS: KARE-) ___
accept: カレーをおねがいします
questions.explanation: カレーにします is the choosing pattern: "I'll go with the curry". カレーをください and カレーをおねがいします are accepted too.

questions.stem: Where do you take off your shoes in a Japanese home?
choices: In the げんかん, before stepping up
At the door of each room
questions.explanation: The げんかん is the lower entry area. Shoes come off there, and you step up onto the raised floor in socks or slippers.

questions.stem: What do you say as you enter a friend's home?
questions.explanation: おじゃまします ("I'm going to disturb you") is what a visitor says. ただいま is for coming home to your own house, いってきます for leaving it, and いらっしゃいませ is what shops say to customers.

questions.stem: Your host's tatami room is next to the corridor. You're wearing the slippers they gave you. What do you do?
choices: Take the slippers off before stepping onto the tatami.
Put your outdoor shoes back on.
questions.explanation: No slippers on たたみ: socks or bare feet only. Slippers are for corridors and wooden floors.

questions.stem: What is the classic visitor's mistake with toilet slippers?
choices: Taking them off at the toilet door
Walking back into the living room still wearing them
questions.explanation: Toilet slippers stay in the toilet room: put them on at the door, and change back when you leave.

questions.stem: How do you use a Japanese family bath?
choices: Wash in the tub with soap, then drain it.
Drain the tub and refill it for yourself.
Soak first, then wash in the tub.
Wash and rinse outside the tub, then soak; leave the water in.
questions.explanation: You wash outside the tub, then get in clean to soak. The water is shared by the family one after another, so no soap goes in and the plug stays in.

questions.stem: What does 2LDK mean in a flat advertisement?
choices: Two rooms plus a living-dining-kitchen area
Two kitchens and a living room
questions.explanation: L is living room, D dining area and K kitchen; the number is how many other rooms there are. A 2LDK has two rooms plus an LDK.

questions.stem: What is a マンション in Japan?
choices: A flat in a large, solid (usually concrete) building
questions.explanation: Despite the English word, a マンション is an apartment in a solid block of flats. A smaller, lighter building is an アパート.

questions.stem: An ad says a bedroom is 6じょう. What does that tell you?
choices: Its size: about six tatami mats, roughly 10 square metres
It is on the sixth floor
questions.explanation: Rooms are measured in じょう, the number of tatami mats they would hold. In rental ads one じょう is at least about 1.6 square metres, so 6じょう is about 10.

questions.stem: Listen. What is the host telling you?

audio.text: どうぞ、あがってください

questions.explanation: あがってください is literally "please step up", from the げんかん onto the raised floor: please come in. It doesn't mean going upstairs here.

questions.stem: Listen. What is the guest asking?

audio.text: おふろにはいってもいいですか

questions.explanation: おふろに{入|はい}る is "take a bath", and 〜てもいいですか asks permission: may I take a bath?

questions.stem: In the morning, where does the ふとん go?
choices: It stays on the floor all day.
questions.explanation: ふとん are laid out at night and folded into the おしいれ, the deep built-in closet, in the morning, so the room can be used by day.

questions.stem: Type the word for "bath" with the polite お, in hiragana: ___
questions.explanation: おふろ: the bath, and also the bathroom where you bathe. The toilet is a separate room, トイレ.

questions.stem: What is the dictionary form of {飲|の}みます (drink)?
questions.explanation: {飲|の}む is group 1: the い-row sound み before ます becomes the う-row sound む. {飲|の}みる treats it as group 2 (stem + る), which is wrong for this verb.

questions.stem: What is the dictionary form of {来|き}ます (come)?
questions.explanation: {来|く}る is irregular (group 3): {来|き}ます, but {来|く}る. きる would be the dictionary form of a group 2 verb (and it's another verb, "to wear"); こる and くう don't exist as forms of this verb.

questions.stem: Which verb is group 2, so its dictionary form is the ます stem + る?
questions.explanation: おきます (get up) is group 2: おきる. The others are group 1: {書|か}く, {買|か}う, とる. The ます form alone doesn't tell you: おきます and {書|か}きます both have き before ます, so learn each verb's group.

questions.stem: Type the dictionary form of {買|か}います (to buy): ___
questions.explanation: {買|か}う. The い before ます becomes う. Not かる or かゆ: an い-row い simply becomes the う-row う.

questions.stem: Type the dictionary form of およぎます (to swim): ___
questions.explanation: およぐ: ぎ (i-row) becomes ぐ (u-row). およぎる would be the group 2 pattern, but およぐ is group 1.

questions.stem: Choose the correct sentence: "I like reading books."
choices: {本|ほん}を{読|よ}むがすきです。
{本|ほん}を{読|よ}むのがすきです。
{本|ほん}が{読|よ}むのをすきです。
{本|ほん}を{読|よ}みますのがすきです。
questions.explanation: A verb needs の before が すき: {読|よ}むのがすきです. The book stays {本|ほん}を, the object of {読|よ}む. The first choice has no の, the third marks the book with が and すき with を, and the last uses the ます form, which can't go before の.

questions.stem: Complete the answer: "しゅみは{何|なん}ですか。" — "しゅみはしゃしんをとる___です。"
questions.explanation: After しゅみは, a verb phrase is turned into a noun with こと: しゃしんをとることです (My hobby is taking photos). の works before すき or じょうず, but not here. もの is a physical thing and ところ a place.

questions.stem: Choose the correct form: "Before I went to Japan, I studied Japanese." — {日本|にほん}へ___まえに、{日本語|にほんご}をべんきょうしました。
questions.explanation: The verb before まえに is always the dictionary form, even when the sentence is about the past: {行|い}くまえに. The past tense is shown by the last verb, しました. ×{行|い}ったまえに is a very common mistake.

questions.stem: What does "ねるまえに、おんがくを{聞|き}きます。" mean?
choices: After I go to bed, I listen to music.
I listen to music while I sleep.
Before I go to bed, I listen to music.
I go to bed before listening to music.
questions.explanation: ねるまえに is "before sleeping / before going to bed", and the main verb {聞|き}きます is what happens first. "After" would be ねたあとで (with the た form).

questions.stem: How is 北 read in "{駅|えき}の北口で{会|あ}いましょう。"?
questions.explanation: 北 is きた (north), and in 北口 (north exit) it's read きたぐち. ひがし is 東, みなみ is 南 and にし is 西.

questions.stem: Which kanji means "west"?
questions.explanation: 西 (にし) is west. 東 (ひがし) is east, 南 (みなみ) is south and 北 (きた) is north. A hint for 東: the sun 日 seen through a tree 木, as at sunrise in the east.

questions.stem: Match each kanji to its reading.
questions.explanation: 東 ひがし (east), 西 にし (west), 南 みなみ (south), 北 きた (north). みぎ and ひだり are right and left (右, 左).

questions.stem: How is 東西南北 (the four directions) read?
choices: ひがしにしみなみきた
questions.explanation: In this compound the kanji take their on'yomi: トウ, ザイ (サイ with a sound change), ナン, ボク (ホク with a sound change): とうざいなんぼく. Notice the order: east, west, south, north.

questions.stem: What is the Japanese word for "northeast"?
questions.explanation: {北東|ほくとう}: like English, north or south comes first. {南西|なんせい} is southwest, {南東|なんとう} southeast and {北西|ほくせい} northwest. (You'll also see {東北|とうほく}, with the kanji the other way round: it's the name of the north-eastern region of Japan's main island.)

questions.stem: Which verb do you use for playing the guitar? ギターを___。
questions.explanation: Instruments you play with your fingers (piano, guitar) take ひく: ギターをひきます. する is for sports and games (テニスをします); あそぶ is "play, have fun" without an object like this.

questions.stem: Read: "わたしのしゅみは{山|やま}にのぼることです。{日曜日|にちようび}は、よく{東|ひがし}の{山|やま}へ{行|い}きます。{山|やま}へ{行|い}くまえに、{駅|えき}でおべんとうを{買|か}います。" What does the writer do before going to the mountains?
choices: Buys a boxed lunch at the station
Climbs a mountain in the east
Meets friends at the east exit
questions.explanation: {山|やま}へ{行|い}くまえに、{駅|えき}でおべんとうを{買|か}います: before going to the mountains, the writer buys a boxed lunch at the station. The east ({東|ひがし}) is where the mountains are, not what happens first.

questions.stem: Listen. What is the speaker's hobby?

audio.text: わたしのしゅみは、ピアノをひくことです。

questions.explanation: The speaker said ピアノをひくこと: playing the piano. ギター would be the guitar; ひく works for both, so listen for the instrument.

questions.stem: Listen. Where will they meet?

audio.text: あした、駅の南口で会いましょう。

questions.explanation: The speaker said みなみぐち ({南口|みなみぐち}), the south exit. The others would be きたぐち, ひがしぐち and にしぐち.

questions.stem: Listen and type the verb you hear, in hiragana: ___

audio.text: あつめる

questions.explanation: あつめる (to collect), a group 2 verb: ます form あつめます.

questions.stem: Is "{本|ほん}を{読|よ}むのがすきです。" polite or casual?
choices: Casual, because {読|よ}む is a plain form
Polite, because the sentence ends with です
Rude: plain forms are never used with です
Casual, because すき is an adjective
questions.explanation: The last word decides: the sentence ends with です, so it's polite. The plain form {読|よ}む is required inside the pattern 〜のがすきです and doesn't make the sentence casual.

questions.stem: What is the ない form of {書|か}く (write)?
questions.explanation: {書|か}く is group 1: く (u-row) becomes か (a-row) + ない: {書|か}かない. {書|か}きない uses the ます stem, and {書|か}くない treats the verb like an い-adjective.

questions.stem: What is the ない form of {買|か}う (buy)?
questions.explanation: Verbs ending in う take わ, not あ: {買|か}わない. ×{買|か}あない is the most common mistake; {買|か}らない and {買|か}いない aren't forms of {買|か}う.

questions.stem: What is the ない form of {来|く}る (come)?
questions.explanation: {来|く}る is irregular: its vowel changes to お, こない, written {来|こ}ない. The kanji stays the same, so read it from the ending: {来|く}る, {来|き}ます, {来|こ}ない.

questions.stem: What is the plain negative of ある (there is)?
questions.explanation: ある is the one verb whose ない form is just ない: お{金|かね}がない (I have no money). ×あらない follows the group 1 rule, but it doesn't exist.

questions.stem: Type the ない form of {飲|の}む (to drink): ___
questions.explanation: {飲|の}まない: む becomes ま, then ない.

questions.stem: Type the ない form of する (to do): ___
questions.explanation: する is irregular: しない. The same goes for every する verb: しんぱいしない, べんきょうしない.

questions.stem: かえる (to go home) is a group 1 verb. What is its ない form?
questions.explanation: As a group 1 verb, かえる changes る to ら: かえらない. ×かえない is what a group 2 verb would do; かえる only looks like one. はしる and {入|はい}る work the same way.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "Please don't take photos here."?
choices: ここでしゃしんをとらないでください。
ここでしゃしんをとってないでください。
ここでしゃしんをとりないでください。
ここでしゃしんをとらなくてください。
questions.explanation: "Please don't" is the ない form + でください: とらないでください. It is not built from the て form (とって) or the ます stem (とり), and なくて + ください isn't a pattern.

questions.stem: What does "くつをぬがなくてもいいです。" mean?
choices: You must not take off your shoes.
You don't have to take off your shoes.
May I take off my shoes?
questions.explanation: 〜なくてもいいです is "you don't have to": it's all right even if you don't take them off. "You must not" would be ぬいではいけません; "please take them off" is ぬいでください.

questions.stem: Complete: "You don't have to come tomorrow." — あした___もいいですよ。
questions.explanation: Take the ない form {来|こ}ない, change い to くて: {来|こ}なくて, then もいいです. {来|こ}ないで goes with ください (please don't come), and the ない form of {来|く}る starts with こ, not き.

questions.stem: You see the sign "きんえん" in a station. What does it mean?
questions.explanation: きんえん is "no smoking". Danger is きけん or あぶない, caution is ちゅうい and the entrance is {入口|いりぐち}.

questions.stem: A sign in a museum says "Please don't touch." Which is it?
choices: さわらないでください
さわらなくてもいいです
questions.explanation: さわらないでください: please don't touch. さわってください asks you to touch, さわってもいいです allows it, and さわらなくてもいいです says you don't have to touch it.

questions.stem: Read the park rules: "・ごみはもちかえりましょう。・{花|はな}にさわらないでください。・ペットといっしょに{入|はい}ってもいいです。・じてんしゃはここにとめないでください。" Which of these is allowed?
choices: Bringing a pet into the park
questions.explanation: ペットといっしょに{入|はい}ってもいいです: you may come in with a pet. Rubbish should be taken home (もちかえりましょう), and touching the flowers and parking bikes here are asked against with ないでください.

questions.stem: A student asks: "{先生|せんせい}、きょう、しゅくだいをしなくてもいいですか。" The teacher says it's fine not to. What does the teacher say?
choices: いいえ、しなくてもいいです。
はい、しなくてもいいですよ。
はい、してはいけません。
いいえ、しないでください。
questions.explanation: はい agrees with the question ("Yes, it's fine if you don't"), and the answer repeats the pattern: しなくてもいいですよ. いいえ would disagree, and してはいけません (you must not do it) and しないでください (please don't) are about forbidding it, not about not having to.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "You must not eat here."?
choices: ここで{食|た}べなくてもいいです。
ここで{食|た}べてもいいです。
ここで{食|た}べないです。
ここで{食|た}べてはいけません。
questions.explanation: 〜てはいけません (Lesson 19) forbids: {食|た}べてはいけません. {食|た}べなくてもいいです means "you don't have to eat", {食|た}べてもいいです "you may eat", and {食|た}べないです simply "(I) don't eat".

questions.stem: Match each dictionary form to its ない form.
questions.explanation: {書|か}く → {書|か}かない and {話|はな}す → {話|はな}さない (group 1: u-row to a-row); {見|み}る → {見|み}ない (group 2: る → ない); する → しない. ×{見|み}らない treats {見|み}る as group 1.

questions.stem: Listen. What are you asked not to do?

audio.text: ここでたばこをすわないでください。

questions.explanation: たばこをすわないでください: please don't smoke. すう is "to smoke" (ない form すわない, with わ because it ends in う).

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker tell you?

audio.text: あしたは来なくてもいいですよ。

choices: You don't have to come tomorrow.
questions.explanation: {来|こ}なくてもいいです: you don't have to come. "Please don't come" would be {来|こ}ないでください, and "please come" {来|き}てください.

questions.stem: Listen and type the word you hear, in hiragana: ___

audio.text: わすれない

questions.explanation: わすれない, the ない form of わすれる (to forget, group 2): "don't forget".

questions.stem: Which is a correct polite way to say "I don't eat meat."? (にく = meat)
choices: にくを{食|た}べないます。
にくを{食|た}べませんです。
にくを{食|た}べなかったです。
にくを{食|た}べないです。
questions.explanation: ない is like an い-adjective, so add です: {食|た}べないです, which means the same as {食|た}べません. ×{食|た}べないます and ×{食|た}べませんです stack two endings, and {食|た}べなかったです is past: "I didn't eat".

questions.stem: What is the た form of {飲|の}む (drink)?
questions.explanation: Verbs ending in む, ぶ, ぬ have the て form んで, so the た form is んだ: {飲|の}んだ. ×{飲|の}みた is the group 2 pattern; った is for う, つ, る and いた for く.

questions.stem: What is the た form of {行|い}く (go)?
questions.explanation: {行|い}く is the exception among く verbs: {行|い}って, so {行|い}った. ×{行|い}いた is what the regular く rule would give ({書|か}く → {書|か}いた).

questions.stem: What is the た form of およぐ (swim)?
questions.explanation: ぐ verbs have the て form いで, so the た form is いだ: およいだ. Only く verbs end in いた.

questions.stem: Type the た form of {書|か}く (to write): ___
questions.explanation: {書|か}いた: the て form is {書|か}いて, so て becomes た.

questions.stem: Type the た form of {来|く}る (to come): ___
questions.explanation: {来|き}た, from the て form {来|き}て. The kanji is read き here, as in {来|き}ます.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "Have you ever been to Hokkaido?"
choices: ほっかいどうへ{行|い}くことがありますか。
ほっかいどうへ{行|い}ったことをありますか。
ほっかいどうへ{行|い}ったことがありますか。
ほっかいどうへ{行|い}きましたことがありますか。
questions.explanation: Experience is the た form + ことがあります: {行|い}ったことがありますか. The dictionary form ({行|い}くこと) talks about something that sometimes happens, ある takes が (not を), and the ます form can't go before こと.

questions.stem: Which sentence is NOT natural?
choices: きのう、すしを{食|た}べたことがあります。
すしを{食|た}べたことがあります。
きのう、すしを{食|た}べました。
すしを{食|た}べたことがありません。
questions.explanation: 〜たことがあります is about life experience, so it doesn't go with a specific time like きのう. For one recent event, use the past: きのう、すしを{食|た}べました.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "On my days off I do things like reading and watching films."?
choices: {休|やす}みの{日|ひ}は、{本|ほん}を{読|よ}んで、えいがを{見|み}ます。
{休|やす}みの{日|ひ}は、{本|ほん}を{読|よ}んだり、えいがを{見|み}たり。
{休|やす}みの{日|ひ}は、{本|ほん}を{読|よ}みましたり、えいがを{見|み}ましたりします。
{休|やす}みの{日|ひ}は、{本|ほん}を{読|よ}んだり、えいがを{見|み}たりします。
questions.explanation: Each example verb is the plain た form + り, and the sentence ends with する: {読|よ}んだり、 {見|み}たりします. The first is a て-form sequence (I read, then watch), the second lacks the final する, and たり never follows a ます form.

questions.stem: What does "りょこうで、{山|やま}にのぼったり、おんせんに{入|はい}ったりしました。" mean?
choices: On the trip, we climbed a mountain and then went in a hot spring.
On the trip, we want to climb mountains and go in hot springs.
On the trip, we did things like climbing mountains and going in hot springs.
We have never climbed a mountain or been in a hot spring.
questions.explanation: たり〜たりしました gives examples of what was done, in no particular order ("things like …"). A fixed order ("and then") would be the て form: のぼって、{入|はい}りました.

questions.stem: A: "おんせんに{入|はい}ったことがありますか。" B says yes. What does B say?
questions.explanation: The short answer uses ある: はい、あります (No: いいえ、ありません). はい、{入|はい}ります means "I'll go in", ×{入|はい}ったです isn't polite Japanese, and こと isn't repeated on its own.

questions.stem: Complete: "I've never been there, not even once." — いちども{行|い}ったことが___。
questions.explanation: いちども + negative is "never, not once": いちども{行|い}ったことがありません. あります would contradict いちども.

questions.stem: What is the plain past negative of {食|た}べる ("didn't eat")?
questions.explanation: ない changes like an い-adjective: ない → なかった, so {食|た}べない → {食|た}べなかった. The polite version is {食|た}べませんでした.

questions.stem: Read: "{先週|せんしゅう}、{友|とも}だちとほっかいどうへりょこうに{行|い}きました。りょかんにとまりました。{毎日|まいにち}、{山|やま}をあるいたり、しゃしんをとったりしました。よるは、はじめておんせんに{入|はい}りました。" Where did the writer stay?
questions.explanation: りょかんにとまりました: they stayed at a ryokan, a Japanese-style inn. とまる here is "to stay overnight".

questions.stem: Read the same text again: "{先週|せんしゅう}、{友|とも}だちとほっかいどうへりょこうに{行|い}きました。りょかんにとまりました。{毎日|まいにち}、{山|やま}をあるいたり、しゃしんをとったりしました。よるは、はじめておんせんに{入|はい}りました。" What did the writer do for the first time?
questions.explanation: はじめておんせんに{入|はい}りました: they went in a hot spring for the first time. The walking and photos were examples of what they did every day (たり).

questions.stem: What is a りょかん?
questions.explanation: A りょかん is a traditional Japanese inn, often with tatami rooms and a bath. A temple is おてら, a souvenir おみやげ and a hot spring おんせん.

questions.stem: Match each dictionary form to its た form.
questions.explanation: す → した, う → った, ぶ → んだ, く → いた: the same sound rules as the て form. ×{買|か}いた would be "wrote" ({書|か}いた), a different verb.

questions.stem: Listen. What has the speaker done?

audio.text: おんせんにはいったことがあります。

questions.explanation: おんせんに{入|はい}ったことがあります: "I've been in a hot spring (at some point)".

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker do on Sundays?

audio.text: 日曜日は、テニスをしたり、買いものをしたりします。

choices: Tennis, then shopping, always in that order
questions.explanation: 〜たり〜たりします lists examples: tennis, shopping and so on. It doesn't fix an order, and it says there's more than just tennis.

questions.stem: Listen and type the verb you hear, in hiragana: ___

audio.text: とまった

questions.explanation: とまった, the た form of とまる (to stay overnight, or to stop): る → った.

questions.stem: After a long walk you want to say "I'm tired." Which is natural?
questions.explanation: つかれる means "to get tired", so "I'm tired (now)" is the past, つかれました: I got tired and still am. つかれます would mean "I (will) get tired".

questions.stem: You ask a close friend "Are you going?" casually. Which is most natural?
questions.explanation: A casual question is the plain form with a rising voice: {行|い}く？ か at the end sounds rough in casual speech, だ never goes in a question, and {行|い}きます is the polite form.

questions.stem: What is the casual (plain) version of "{高|たか}いです"?
questions.explanation: An い-adjective just drops です: {高|たか}い. ×{高|たか}いだ is a classic mistake: い-adjectives never take だ.

questions.stem: What is the plain form of "しずかでした" (it was quiet)?
questions.explanation: For な-adjectives and nouns, でした becomes だった: しずかだった. ×しずかかった uses the い-adjective ending, and しずかだ is non-past.

questions.stem: What is the plain negative of いい (good)?
questions.explanation: いい changes to よ- in its other forms: よくない, よかった, よくなかった. ×いくない is a common mistake.

questions.stem: Type the plain form of {行|い}きませんでした (didn't go): ___
questions.explanation: The ない form {行|い}かない, with ない → なかった: {行|い}かなかった.

questions.stem: Type the casual word for "yes, yeah" in hiragana: ___
questions.explanation: うん is the casual はい. Be careful: ううん (two u's, with a dip in the voice) means "no".

questions.stem: With whom is casual speech the most natural choice?
choices: A teacher you have just met
questions.explanation: Family and close friends get casual speech. Shop staff, a boss and a teacher you've just met get です/ます; casual speech to them would sound rude.

questions.stem: Your friend has forgotten about tomorrow's test. Which sentence tells them, as new information?
choices: あしたはテストでしょうか。
questions.explanation: よ gives the listener something new: "There's a test tomorrow, you know." ね would treat it as something you both already know; でしょうか wonders whether it's so.

questions.stem: You and a friend step outside into the cold. Complete: "さむい___。" (It's cold, isn't it?)
questions.explanation: ね shares a feeling you both have: さむいね. よ would tell the friend as if they didn't know, and ×さむいだ is wrong (い-adjectives don't take だ).

questions.stem: A weather forecast: "It will probably rain tomorrow." — あしたは{雨|あめ}___。
questions.explanation: A noun goes straight before でしょう, without だ: {雨|あめ}でしょう. だろう is the casual version, so it doesn't combine with です.

questions.stem: Casually, "Are you free?" is:
questions.explanation: In casual questions だ is always dropped: ひま？ ×ひまだ？ sounds wrong, ひまか？ is rough, and ひまです？ mixes in the polite form without か.

questions.stem: A friend says "いっしょに{行|い}かない？" What do they mean?
choices: Do you want to go together?
questions.explanation: A plain negative question is a casual invitation, like 〜ませんか: "Won't you come along?" The answer is うん、{行|い}く！ or ごめん、ちょっと….

questions.stem: A friend asks "きのうのパーティー、どうだった？" Which casual reply is correct?
questions.explanation: The past of the い-adjective たのしい is たのしかった, and よ makes it a friendly answer. An い-adjective never takes でした, だ or だった.

questions.stem: A: "あした、ひま？" B: "ううん、いそがしい。" What does B mean?
choices: Yes, but only in the afternoon.
questions.explanation: ううん is the casual "no", and いそがしい is "busy". Don't mix it up with うん (yes).

questions.stem: Read the messages: "はると：あした、えいが{見|み}に{行|い}かない？ / さくら：ごめん、あしたはアルバイト。{日曜日|にちようび}は？ / はると：いいよ。じゃあ、{日曜日|にちようび}ね。" When will they go to the cinema?
questions.explanation: Sakura has work (アルバイト) tomorrow and suggests Sunday; Haruto agrees with いいよ and confirms {日曜日|にちようび}ね.

questions.stem: Which sentence is incorrect?
questions.explanation: ×{行|い}くですか mixes a plain verb with です. A verb is polite as {行|い}きますか and casual as {行|い}く？; {行|い}かない？ is a casual invitation.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker mean?

audio.text: これ、おいしいね。

questions.explanation: おいしいね: "It's good, isn't it?" ね asks the listener to share the feeling. A question would rise without ね (おいしい？), and the past would be おいしかった.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the forecast say?

audio.text: あしたは雨でしょう。

questions.explanation: {雨|あめ}でしょう: "it will probably rain". あした is tomorrow.

questions.stem: Listen. What happened?

audio.text: ごめん、きのう行かなかった。

questions.explanation: {行|い}かなかった is the plain past negative: "didn't go". ごめん is a casual "sorry".

questions.stem: Match each casual phrase to its polite version.
questions.explanation: Casual questions drop か and use the plain form; うん is はい; わかった is the plain past of わかる. いいえ matches ううん, which isn't in the list.

questions.stem: Which phrase means "the book I bought yesterday"?
choices: きのう{買|か}った{本|ほん}
きのう{買|か}いました{本|ほん}
きのう{買|か}ったの{本|ほん}
questions.explanation: The describing clause comes before the noun, in a plain form, touching it directly: きのう{買|か}った{本|ほん}. It never follows the noun, never uses ます, and no の goes between a verb and a noun.

questions.stem: What does "めがねをかけている{人|ひと}" mean?
choices: a person who lost their glasses
questions.explanation: めがねをかけている (is wearing glasses, Lesson 17) describes {人|ひと}: "the person who is wearing glasses".

questions.stem: Complete: "the book my father wrote" — {父|ちち} ___ {書|か}いた{本|ほん}
questions.explanation: The doer inside a relative clause takes が (or の): {父|ちち}が{書|か}いた{本|ほん}. は can't be used inside a clause, because it marks the topic of the whole sentence.

questions.stem: Complete: "when I'm free" — ひま___とき
questions.explanation: ひま is a な-adjective, so it takes な before a noun, including とき: ひまなとき. の is for nouns ({子|こ}どものとき), and だ can't go before a noun.

questions.stem: Complete: "when I was a child" — {子|こ}ども___とき
questions.explanation: A noun links to とき with の: {子|こ}どものとき. な is for な-adjectives (ひまなとき).

questions.stem: Which sentence means "When I went to Japan, I went in a hot spring." (in Japan, after arriving)?
choices: {日本|にほん}へ{行|い}くとき、おんせんに{入|はい}りました。
{日本|にほん}へ{行|い}ったとき、おんせんに{入|はい}りました。
{日本|にほん}へ{行|い}ったまえに、おんせんに{入|はい}りました。
{日本|にほん}へ{行|い}きましたとき、おんせんに{入|はい}りました。
questions.explanation: The た form in the とき clause says the going had already happened: {行|い}ったとき. {行|い}くとき would mean "when I was about to go" (before leaving). まえに always takes the dictionary form, and the ます form can't go before とき.

questions.stem: You bought souvenirs at your home airport before flying to Japan. Complete: {日本|にほん}へ___とき、くうこうでおみやげを{買|か}いました。
questions.explanation: You hadn't arrived yet when you bought them, so the clause uses the dictionary form: {行|い}くとき. {行|い}ったとき would place the buying in Japan, after arriving.

questions.stem: Type the word that means "when" in "さむい(…)、おちゃを{飲|の}みます。" (When it's cold, I drink tea.): ___
questions.explanation: とき (also written {時|とき}): さむいとき, "when it's cold". An い-adjective goes straight before it.

questions.stem: Complete "the person who is taking photos over there": あそこでしゃしんをとって(…){人|ひと}. Type the missing word: ___
questions.explanation: In a relative clause, "is doing" is the plain ている form: とっている{人|ひと}. The polite います can't go before a noun.

questions.stem: Which phrase means "the shop I always go to"?
choices: いつも{行|い}きます{店|みせ}
いつも{行|い}くの{店|みせ}
questions.explanation: Plain dictionary form right before the noun: いつも{行|い}く{店|みせ}. The ます form, the English word order and an extra の are all wrong.

questions.stem: What does "これは{友|とも}だちがつくったケーキです。" mean?
choices: This is the cake I made for my friend.
This is the cake my friend made.
My friend is making a cake.
This is my friend's favourite cake.
questions.explanation: {友|とも}だちがつくった describes ケーキ: "the cake (that) my friend made". The friend is the doer, marked with が.

questions.stem: Read: "このしゃしんを{見|み}てください。{左|ひだり}でギターをひいている{人|ひと}は{父|ちち}です。{右|みぎ}でわらっている{人|ひと}は{母|はは}です。" Who is laughing?
questions.explanation: {右|みぎ}でわらっている{人|ひと}は{母|はは}です: the person laughing on the right is the mother. The father is the one playing the guitar on the left.

questions.stem: At the lost-and-found, the station attendant asks: "どんなかばんですか。" What is the best answer?
choices: くろくて{小|ちい}さいかばんです。
かばんをなくしました。
{北口|きたぐち}でみつかりました。
questions.explanation: どんな asks "what kind of": a description answers it, "a small black bag". The other replies don't describe the bag.

questions.stem: In "{父|ちち}の{書|か}いた{本|ほん}" (the book my father wrote), what does の do?
choices: It shows that the book belongs to my father.
It marks the doer in the clause, like が.
It turns {書|か}いた into a noun.
questions.explanation: Inside a relative clause, の can replace が for the doer: {父|ちち}の{書|か}いた{本|ほん} = {父|ちち}が{書|か}いた{本|ほん}. It's about who wrote the book, not who owns it.

questions.stem: What does "こまったとき、{先生|せんせい}に{聞|き}いてください。" mean?
choices: When you're free, please talk to the teacher.
When you're tired, please tell the teacher.
When you're stuck, please ask the teacher.
When the teacher is busy, please wait.
questions.explanation: こまる is "to be in trouble, not know what to do", so こまったとき is "when you're stuck". ひまな とき would be "when you're free".

questions.stem: Match each verb to its meaning.
questions.explanation: なくす (lose), みつける (find), ひろう (pick up), わらう (laugh, smile). "To forget" is わすれる and "to be born" is {生|う}まれる.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker say?

audio.text: きのう買った本はおもしろいです。

choices: The book I bought yesterday is interesting.
I'm going to buy an interesting book tomorrow.
The book I read yesterday was boring.
I didn't buy the book yesterday.
questions.explanation: きのう{買|か}った{本|ほん} (the book I bought yesterday) is the topic, and おもしろいです (is interesting) says something about it.

questions.stem: Listen. Who is Mr Tanaka?

audio.text: めがねをかけている人がたなかさんです。

questions.explanation: めがねをかけている{人|ひと}: the person wearing glasses. A hat would be ぼうしをかぶっている.

questions.stem: Listen. When did the speaker live in Hokkaido?

audio.text: 子どものとき、ほっかいどうにすんでいました。

questions.explanation: {子|こ}どものとき: "when I was a child". すんでいました is "was living".

questions.stem: Which sentence has a mistake?
choices: ひまなとき、ギターをひきます。
さむいとき、おちゃを{飲|の}みます。
{子|こ}どもとき、よくおよぎました。
こまったとき、{先生|せんせい}に{聞|き}きます。
questions.explanation: A noun needs の before とき: {子|こ}どものとき. ひまなとき (な-adjective + な), さむいとき (い-adjective) and こまったとき (verb) are all correct.

questions.stem: Who says "いらっしゃいませ"?
questions.explanation: いらっしゃいませ (Welcome!) is said by staff to customers. Customers don't say it back: a nod is enough.

questions.stem: What does "しょうしょうおまちください。" mean?
questions.explanation: しょうしょう is a formal "a little", and おまちください is the keigo form of まってください: "Please wait a moment." "Thank you for waiting" is おまたせしました.

questions.stem: かしこまりました is the keigo way of saying …
choices: ありがとうございます
questions.explanation: Staff say かしこまりました ("Certainly") where you would say わかりました: I understand and will do it.

questions.stem: めしあがる is the respectful verb for …
questions.explanation: めしあがる is the respectful "eat / drink", used for other people: {何|なに}をめしあがりますか. The respectful verbs for the others are いらっしゃる, ごらんになる and おっしゃる.

questions.stem: いただく (in いただきます) belongs to which kind of keigo?
questions.explanation: いただく is humble: it describes your own action (receiving, eating) modestly. That's why you can say いただきます about yourself but never ×わたしはめしあがります.

questions.stem: Which sentence is wrong?
choices: {先生|せんせい}は{何|なに}をめしあがりますか。
わたしはすしをめしあがります。
どうぞおかけください。
questions.explanation: めしあがる is respectful, for other people's eating; using it about yourself is a mistake. Say わたしはすしを{食|た}べます (or いただきます).

questions.stem: At a café counter you hear: "こちらでおめしあがりですか。" You want to eat there. What do you say?
choices: はい、ここで{食|た}べます。
questions.explanation: Answer keigo with ordinary polite Japanese about yourself: はい、ここで{食|た}べます. めしあがる is for others, and いらっしゃいませ and かしこまりました are what staff say.

questions.stem: A receptionist tells a visitor "きむらはすぐまいります。" about her colleague Mr Kimura. Why no さん?
choices: さん is never used in offices.
Kimura is in her own group (uchi), so she doesn't raise him in front of an outsider.
questions.explanation: Speaking to an outsider (soto), employees treat their own colleagues, even their boss, as part of their uchi: no さん, and humble verbs like まいる. The visitor still says きむらさん.

questions.stem: A shop assistant offers you a bag, and you don't need one. What do you say?
questions.explanation: けっこうです is a polite "No, thank you" (many younger people say だいじょうぶです). The other three are phrases staff use, not customers.

questions.stem: On the platform you hear: "まもなく、{電車|でんしゃ}がまいります。" What does it mean?
questions.explanation: まもなく is "shortly, soon", and まいります is the humble "come", used by the railway about its own train: "The train will be arriving shortly."

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker ask you to do?

audio.text: しょうしょう、おまちください。

questions.explanation: しょうしょうおまちください: please wait a moment. Come in is お{入|はい}りください, have a seat おかけください, be careful ごちゅういください.

questions.stem: Listen. What is the speaker saying?

audio.text: もうしわけありません。

questions.explanation: もうしわけありません is a formal apology, much stronger than すみません. "Thanks for your hard work" is おつかれさまです.

questions.stem: Which word describes heavy, pouring rain?
questions.explanation: ザーザー imitates the sound of heavy rain: {雨|あめ}がザーザーふっています. にこにこ is smiling, ペラペラ fluent and ぐっすり sleeping soundly.

questions.stem: Complete: "Maria speaks fluent Japanese." — マリアさんは{日本語|にほんご}が___です。
questions.explanation: ペラペラ is "fluent". ぺこぺこ looks similar but means "starving"; ドキドキ is a racing heart and キラキラ sparkling.

questions.stem: Complete: "I'm starving." — おなかが___です。
questions.explanation: おなかがぺこぺこです: "my stomach is empty", I'm starving. Read the kana carefully: ペラペラ (fluent) has ら, ぺこぺこ has こ.

questions.stem: What does "しけんのまえは、ドキドキします。" mean?
questions.explanation: ドキドキする is the feeling of your heart pounding: nervous (or thrilled). しけん is an exam.

questions.stem: Which sentence is incorrect?
choices: {日本語|にほんご}がペラペラします。
ゆっくり{話|はな}してください。
questions.explanation: ペラペラ goes with です or with {話|はな}す, not with する: {日本語|にほんご}がペラペラです. ドキドキ and にこにこ take する, and ゆっくり is used as an adverb before a verb.

questions.stem: Which word imitates a real sound (giongo)?
questions.explanation: ワンワン is a dog's bark, a real sound. にこにこ, ゆっくり and キラキラ describe a look, a manner or a state (gitaigo): smiling, slowly, sparkling.

questions.stem: Your host says "どうぞ、ゆっくりしてください。" What do they mean?
questions.explanation: ゆっくりしてください is "relax, take your time, make yourself at home". "Please speak slowly" needs the verb: ゆっくり{話|はな}してください.

questions.stem: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explanation: ワクワク excited, キラキラ sparkling, ぐっすり soundly (of sleep), にこにこ smiling. Fluent is ペラペラ and pouring rain ザーザー.

questions.stem: Type a dog's bark in katakana (use CAPITALS: WANWAN): ___
questions.explanation: ワンワン, usually written in katakana like a sound effect; わんわん in hiragana is also seen.

questions.stem: Listen. What is the weather like?

audio.text: 雨がザーザーふっています。

questions.explanation: ザーザー is heavy rain. Gentle rain would be しとしと.

questions.stem: Listen. How did the speaker sleep?

audio.text: きのうは、ぐっすりねました。

questions.explanation: ぐっすりねる is to sleep soundly: "I slept really well last night."

questions.stem: In "あかちゃんがにこにこ(と)わらっています。", what does にこにこ tell you?
choices: How the baby is smiling: happily, beaming
The sound of the baby crying
questions.explanation: Word + (と) + verb describes how the action is done: the baby is smiling happily. The と is often left out.

questions.stem: {雨|あめ}がふっています___、{出|で}かけません。 Choose the word for the blank (It's raining, so I'm not going out).
questions.explanation: から after a clause gives the reason: "it's raining, so…". けど would mean "but", which makes no sense here; まで is "until" and に can't join two clauses.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "It's Sunday, so the shop is crowded." (casual)?
choices: {日曜日|にちようび}から、{店|みせ}は{人|ひと}が{多|おお}いよ。
{店|みせ}は{人|ひと}が{多|おお}いから、{日曜日|にちようび}だよ。
{日曜日|にちようび}だけど、{店|みせ}は{人|ひと}が{多|おお}いよ。
{日曜日|にちようび}だから、{店|みせ}は{人|ひと}が{多|おお}いよ。
questions.explanation: In plain speech a noun needs だ before から: {日曜日|にちようび}だから. Without だ, {日曜日|にちようび}から means "from Sunday". The second sentence swaps reason and result ("the shop is crowded, so it's Sunday"), and だけど means "but".

questions.stem: 「どうしてきのう{来|き}ませんでしたか。」 Which answer is correct?
choices: あたまがいたかったからです。
あたまがいたいから{来|き}ます。
あたまがいたかったまでです。
あたまがいたかったけどです。
questions.explanation: To answer どうして (why), give the reason in the plain form followed by からです: いたかったからです, "because I had a headache". The second answer talks about coming, not about yesterday; まで and けど don't give reasons.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "It's got cold."?
questions.explanation: With an い-adjective, change the final い to く and add なる: さむい → さむくなりました. に is only for な-adjectives and nouns, so さむいになりました is wrong, and the い must go: not さむいく.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "The room became quiet."?
choices: へやがしずかくなりました。
へやがしずかなりました。
へやがしずかになりました。
へやがしずかでなりました。
questions.explanation: しずか is a な-adjective, so it takes に before なる: しずかになりました. The く ending is only for い-adjectives, and なる can't follow しずか directly or with で.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "My cold has got better."?
choices: かぜがいくなりました。
かぜがいいになりました。
かぜがよいになりました。
かぜがよくなりました。
questions.explanation: いい uses the stem よ in its other forms, as in よくない and よかった, so "get better" is よくなる. いくなる doesn't exist, and いい is an い-adjective, so it never takes に before なる.

questions.stem: Type the missing particle in kana: {先生|せんせい}___なりたいです。 (I want to become a teacher.)
questions.explanation: A noun takes に before なる: {先生|せんせい}になる, "to become a teacher". With たい it becomes {先生|せんせい}になりたいです.

questions.stem: 「もうひるごはんを{食|た}べましたか。」 How do you say "No, not yet."?
choices: いいえ、{食|た}べませんでした。
questions.explanation: "Not yet" is まだです. いいえ、{食|た}べませんでした means "No, I didn't eat (then)", as if the chance were over. もうです isn't used, and はい would mean "yes".

questions.stem: What does 「いもうとはまだねています。」 mean?
choices: My little sister is already asleep.
My little sister is still asleep.
My little sister isn't asleep any more.
My little sister hasn't slept yet.
questions.explanation: まだ with an affirmative verb means "still": まだねています, "is still sleeping". "Already" would be もう, and "not any more" would be もうねていません.

questions.stem: What does 「この{車|くるま}にはもうのりません。」 mean?
choices: I'll ride in this car again soon.
I still ride in this car.
I don't ride in this car any more.
I haven't ridden in this car yet.
questions.explanation: もう with a negative verb means "not any more". "Still" would be まだ with an affirmative, and "not yet" would be まだ with a negative.

questions.stem: {来年|らいねん}、{日本|にほん}へ___つもりです。 Choose the form (I'm planning to go to Japan next year).
questions.explanation: つもり comes after the dictionary form: {行|い}くつもりです. The ます form can't go before つもり, the て form is for requests and sequences, and {行|い}ったつもり would mean something quite different ("I thought I had gone").

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I'm planning not to drink alcohol today."?
choices: {今日|きょう}はおさけを{飲|の}まないつもりです。
{今日|きょう}はおさけを{飲|の}みませんつもりです。
{今日|きょう}はおさけを{飲|の}みたくないつもりです。
{今日|きょう}はおさけを{飲|の}まなかったつもりです。
questions.explanation: For a plan not to do something, use the ない form before つもり: {飲|の}まないつもりです. ません can't go before つもり, and the past or the たい form don't express a plan.

questions.stem: What does 「このレストランは{高|たか}いですけど、おいしいです。」 mean?
choices: This restaurant is expensive, so the food is good.
This restaurant is expensive, but the food is good.
This restaurant isn't expensive, and the food is good.
Because the food is good, this restaurant is expensive.
questions.explanation: けど means "but": the two clauses contrast. "So" would be から, and nothing in the sentence is negative.

questions.stem: {雨|あめ}です。___、{出|で}かけません。 Choose the word that starts the second sentence (It's raining. So I'm not going out.).
questions.explanation: だから starts a sentence with "so" and points back to the reason before it. けど means "but", and まだ and もう are "still" and "already".

questions.stem: Read: 「わたしは{三年前|さんねんまえ}に{日本|にほん}へ{来|き}ました。はじめは{日本語|にほんご}がぜんぜんわかりませんでした。でも、{毎日|まいにち}べんきょうしましたから、だんだん{上手|じょうず}になりました。」 Why did the writer's Japanese get better?
choices: Because they came to Japan three years ago.
Because they understood nothing at first.
Because they work at a Japanese company.
questions.explanation: The reason is the clause before から: {毎日|まいにち}べんきょうしましたから, "because I studied every day". The other facts are in the text (or not at all, like the company) but aren't given as the reason. だんだん{上手|じょうず}になりました is "gradually got better".

questions.stem: How is 上手 read in "{日本語|にほんご}が上手になりましたね。"?
questions.explanation: 上手 is read じょうず, "good at", a reading of the whole word. へた (bad at) is its opposite and is written 下手; うえて and じょうて just put single readings together.

questions.stem: Listen. What did the speaker say?

audio.text: もうすぐはるですね。

questions.explanation: The speaker said もうすぐはるですね: もうすぐ is "soon, almost". "It's already spring" would be もうはるです, and "not yet" would be まだはるじゃありません.

questions.stem: Listen. What is the speaker asking?

audio.text: どうしてきのう来ませんでしたか。

questions.explanation: どうして means "why": どうしてきのう{来|き}ませんでしたか, "Why didn't you come yesterday?" "How" would be どうやって, and a yes-or-no question would have no question word.

questions.stem: Listen and type what you hear, in kana: ___

audio.text: まだです。

questions.explanation: まだです, "not yet": the natural short answer to a もう…ましたか question.

questions.stem: Match each sentence to its meaning.
left: まだ{食|た}べていません。
questions.explanation: もう + affirmative: already. もう + negative: not any more. まだ + affirmative: still. まだ + negative: not yet.

questions.stem: しんごう___わたってください。 Choose the particle (Please cross at the lights).
questions.explanation: The place you cross takes を, the particle for the route: しんごうをわたる, {道|みち}をわたる. に would mark a destination and で a place where an action happens, not the thing you cross.

questions.stem: かどを{右|みぎ}___まがってください。 Choose the particle (Please turn right at the corner).
questions.explanation: The direction you turn to takes に: {右|みぎ}にまがる. The corner itself already has を. で and の don't mark a direction.

questions.stem: What is the て form of まがる (to turn)?
questions.explanation: まがる is a group 1 verb even though it ends in る, so る becomes って: まがって. まがて would be the pattern for group 2 verbs; まがりて and まがんで aren't forms.

questions.stem: Type the て form of わたる (to cross), in kana: ___
questions.explanation: わたる is group 1, like まがる and かえる, so its て form is わたって (not わたて).

questions.stem: How do you say "the second corner"?
questions.explanation: An ordinal is number + counter + {目|め}: {二|ふた}つ{目|め}, "the second". Without the counter (*{二|に}{目|め}) it's wrong; {二|ふた}つのかど is "two corners", and {二|に}かい is the second floor.

questions.stem: {駅|えき}まであるいて{十分|じゅっぷん}___です。 Choose the word (It's about ten minutes on foot to the station).
questions.explanation: ぐらい (くらい) is "about" for an amount or a length of time: {十分|じゅっぷん}ぐらい. ごろ is "about" for a point in time ({三時|さんじ}ごろ), まで is "until" and め makes ordinals.

questions.stem: Which word is the standard "about" for a clock time, as in "at about three o'clock"?
questions.explanation: For a point in time, use ごろ: {三時|さんじ}ごろ. ぐらい is for amounts and durations ({五分|ごふん}ぐらい), although you'll hear it with clock times in casual speech. つぎ is "next" and むこう "the other side".

questions.stem: A station worker says 「{出口|でぐち}はあちらです。」 What does it mean?
choices: The exit is over that way.
questions.explanation: あちら is the polite word for あそこ, "over there, that way". "Right here" would be こちら, and a question would end in か.

questions.stem: You want to ask how to get to the station. Which question is correct?
choices: すみません、{駅|えき}をどうやって{行|い}きますか。
すみません、{駅|えき}はどうやってですか。
すみません、{駅|えき}までどうやって{行|い}きますか。
すみません、{駅|えき}までどこ{行|い}きますか。
questions.explanation: どうやって asks "how, by what way", and まで marks the destination: {駅|えき}までどうやって{行|い}きますか. を would make the station the route, not the goal; どうやってですか has no verb, and どこ asks "where".

questions.stem: A stranger asks you 「すみません、{駅|えき}はどこですか。」, but you don't know. What is the polite reply?
choices: いいえ、{駅|えき}じゃありません。
すみません、ちょっとわかりません。
questions.explanation: すみません、ちょっとわかりません is "Sorry, I'm not sure", the polite way to say you don't know. いいえ、{駅|えき}じゃありません means "No, it isn't a station"; repeating the question doesn't help, and どういたしまして answers thanks.

questions.stem: What does 「まっすぐ{行|い}って、こうさてんを{左|ひだり}にまがってください。」 mean?
choices: Go straight on, then turn left at the crossroads.
Go straight past the crossroads, then turn right.
Turn left, then go straight to the crossroads.
Cross at the crossroads and go straight on.
questions.explanation: The て form joins steps in order: first まっすぐ{行|い}って (go straight), then こうさてんを{左|ひだり}にまがって (turn left at the crossroads). {左|ひだり} is left, not right, and まがる is "turn", not "cross".

questions.stem: What does 「ぎんこうはしんごうのむこうです。」 mean?
choices: The bank is next to the lights.
The bank is on the other side of the lights.
The bank is just before the lights.
The bank is at the lights.
questions.explanation: むこう is "the other side, beyond": しんごうのむこう is past the lights. "Next to" would be となり.

questions.stem: How is 右 read in "右がわにあります。"?
questions.explanation: On its own, and in 右がわ (the right side), 右 is read みぎ. ひだり is 左 (left). う and ゆう are on'yomi used in compounds, not here.

questions.stem: How is 北口 read in "北口を{出|で}てください。"?
questions.explanation: 北口 is きたぐち, the north exit: きた (north) + くち (mouth, opening), which becomes ぐち in the compound. みなみぐち is the south exit, 南口.

questions.stem: Read: 「{駅|えき}の{東口|ひがしぐち}を{出|で}て、まっすぐ{行|い}ってください。{二|ふた}つ{目|め}のしんごうを{右|みぎ}にまがって、はしをわたってください。としょかんは{左|ひだり}がわにあります。」 What do you do right after turning right?
questions.explanation: The steps are: leave by the east exit, go straight, turn right at the second lights, then はしをわたって, cross the bridge. The library is on the left (it's not a turn), and the turn is at the second set of lights, not the first.

questions.stem: Read: 「ゆうびんきょくですか。この{道|みち}をまっすぐ{行|い}って、{一|ひと}つ{目|め}のかどを{左|ひだり}にまがってください。こうえんのとなりですよ。あるいて{三分|さんぷん}ぐらいです。」 How long does it take to the post office?
questions.explanation: あるいて{三分|さんぷん}ぐらい is "about three minutes on foot". By car would be {車|くるま}で, and a clock time would use {時|じ} and ごろ.

questions.stem: Listen. What should you do?

audio.text: つぎのかどを左にまがってください。

choices: Turn right at the next corner.
Go straight past the next corner.
Turn left at the next corner.
Turn left at the second corner.
questions.explanation: つぎのかどを{左|ひだり}にまがってください: つぎ is "next" and {左|ひだり} is left. The second corner would be {二|ふた}つ{目|め}のかど.

questions.stem: Listen. What should you do?

audio.text: まっすぐ行って、しんごうをわたってください。

choices: Go straight on and cross at the lights.
questions.explanation: まっすぐ{行|い}って、しんごうをわたってください: go straight, then cross at the lights. わたる is "to cross", not "to turn" (まがる).

questions.stem: Listen and type the word you hear, in kana: ___

audio.text: こうばん

questions.explanation: こうばん is a police box. Note the long vowel: こう, two beats.

questions.stem: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explanation: まっすぐ (straight on), まがる (to turn), わたる (to cross), かど (corner), しんごう (traffic lights). "Bridge" would be はし.

questions.stem: A notice says: 「{11月3日|じゅういちがつみっか}（{月|げつ}）から{5日|いつか}（{水|すい}）まで、としょかんは{休|やす}みです。」 Can you borrow a book on 4 November?
choices: No: the library is closed from the 3rd to the 5th.
Yes: it is closed only on Monday.
questions.explanation: から…まで is "from … to": the library is closed (お{休|やす}み) from Monday the 3rd to Wednesday the 5th, so the 4th is included. Nothing says it opens on Wednesday or in the morning.

questions.stem: A message says: 「ゆいさんへ　あしたの{会|かい}は{午後|ごご}{三時|さんじ}からでしたが、{四時|よじ}からになりました。やまだ」 When does the meeting start now?
questions.explanation: 〜でしたが、〜になりました signals a change: it was from three, but it has become from four. The new time counts. {午後|ごご} is p.m.

questions.stem: A menu says: 「コーヒー　400{円|えん}　ケーキ　450{円|えん}　ケーキセット（ケーキとコーヒー）　700{円|えん}」 How much do you save with the cake set?
questions.explanation: Coffee and cake separately cost 400 + 450 = 850 yen; the set is 700 yen, so you save 150 yen.

questions.stem: A sign says: 「ここでたばこをすわないでください。」 What does it mean?
questions.explanation: The end of the sentence decides: 〜ないでください is "please don't". "You may" would be すってもいいです, and "please smoke" すってください.

questions.stem: In a Japanese notice or menu, what does a line starting with ※ usually hold?
choices: An extra note, often an exception
questions.explanation: ※ (こめじるし) works like an asterisk: it adds a note, such as a rule, a time limit or an exception. Always read the ※ lines.

questions.stem: A notice gives the date 11月3日. How is 3日 read?
questions.explanation: The 3rd of the month is みっか, one of the special date readings (Lesson 9). さんにち is a mistake learners make by reading the numbers regularly; みつか misses the small っ.

questions.stem: A calendar page shows 1日 for the first day of the month. How is it read?
questions.explanation: As a date, 1日 is ついたち. いちにち means "one day (long)", as in いちにちじゅう (all day), not the first of the month.

questions.stem: A timetable says: 「{日本語|にほんご}クラス　{火|か}・{木|もく}　18:00〜19:30　※{10日|とおか}（{木|もく}）は{休|やす}みです。」 What happens on Thursday the 10th?
choices: The class is longer than usual.
questions.explanation: The ※ line says {10日|とおか}（{木|もく}）は{休|やす}みです: there's no class that day. The time in the table is the usual one, which doesn't apply to the 10th.

questions.stem: A note says: 「あしたは{来|こ}ないでください。」 What does it mean?
questions.explanation: {来|こ}ないでください is the ない form of {来|く}る plus でください: "please don't come". Read to the end of the sentence: {来|き}てください would be "please come".

questions.stem: A note on the fridge says: 「{母|はは}は{七時|しちじ}ごろかえります。カレーがありますから、{先|さき}に{食|た}べてください。」 What should Yui do?
choices: Eat the curry without waiting for her mother.
questions.explanation: {先|さき}に{食|た}べてください is "please eat first (ahead of me)". The curry is already there (カレーがあります), so there's nothing to make or buy, and waiting is the opposite of the request.

questions.stem: What is an おしらせ?
questions.explanation: おしらせ is a notice or announcement, the word at the top of many signs and letters. A menu is メニュー, a schedule よてい and a train timetable じこくひょう.

questions.stem: On a notice, which word means "place, venue"?
questions.explanation: ばしょ is the place where something happens: ばしょは{駅|えき}の{前|まえ}です. よてい is a schedule, ページ a page and メール an email.

questions.stem: Type the word for "email" in katakana (type it in CAPITALS, with - for the long vowel): ___
questions.explanation: メール (from English "mail") is the everyday word for email, and also for a message on a phone. The long vowel is written with ー.

questions.stem: Read: 「やまださん　こんにちは。エマです。きのうはありがとうございました。{駅|えき}の{前|まえ}のレストランはとてもおいしかったです。また{行|い}きましょう。エマ」 Why is Emma writing?
choices: To invite Yamada for the first time
To ask the way to a restaurant
questions.explanation: きのうはありがとうございました thanks Yamada for yesterday, and the rest says the restaurant was good. また{行|い}きましょう is "let's go again", so it isn't a first invitation.

questions.stem: A poster says: 「ピアノのコンサート　{土曜日|どようび}　{午後|ごご}{二時|にじ}から　※{雨|あめ}の{日|ひ}は{日曜日|にちようび}になります。」 It rains on Saturday. When is the concert?
questions.explanation: The ※ note says that on a rainy day it becomes ({日曜日|にちようび}になります) Sunday. Nothing says it is cancelled, and {午後|ごご} is p.m.

questions.stem: A sign on a door says 入口. What does it mean?
questions.explanation: 入口 (いりぐち) is "entrance": 入 (enter) + 口 (opening). The exit is 出口 (でぐち).

questions.stem: You want to leave the building. Which sign do you follow?
questions.explanation: 出口 (でぐち) is the exit: 出 means "go out". 入口 is the entrance, 北口 the north exit of a station (fine, but not "the way out" in general), and 人口 (じんこう) means "population".

questions.stem: Listen. What time does the library open?

audio.text: としょかんは十時にあきます。

questions.explanation: としょかんは{十時|じゅうじ}にあきます: it opens (あく) at ten. Don't confuse じゅうじ (10:00) with じゅうにじ (12:00).

questions.stem: Listen. What is the speaker asking?

audio.text: このメールを読んでください。

questions.explanation: このメールを{読|よ}んでください: {読|よ}む is "to read". "Write" would be {書|か}いて.

questions.stem: Listen and type the word you hear, in hiragana: ___

audio.text: おしらせ

questions.explanation: おしらせ, "notice, announcement".

questions.stem: Your friend says 「{今日|きょう}はさむいですね。」 What is the natural reply?
questions.explanation: そうですね agrees with something you both know: "It is, isn't it." そうですか takes in news you didn't know, which sounds odd about the weather you're both standing in. ちがいます would contradict, and もしもし is for the phone.

questions.stem: A colleague tells you something you didn't know: 「{来月|らいげつ}、{日本|にほん}へ{行|い}きます。」 Which reaction fits?
questions.explanation: へえ and そうですか show surprised interest in new information. そうですね would agree as if you already knew; ちがいます contradicts, and しつれいします is for leaving or ending a call.

questions.stem: While you explain a plan, a Japanese listener keeps saying はい、はい. What does this most likely mean?
questions.explanation: As aizuchi, はい means "I'm listening, go on", not "I agree". Don't take it as acceptance of your plan.

questions.stem: You didn't catch what someone said. What do you say?
choices: すみません、もういちどおねがいします。
すみません、もう{一|ひと}つください。
questions.explanation: もういちどおねがいします is "once more, please". もう{一|ひと}つください asks for one more thing (in a shop); どういたしまして answers thanks, and よかったですね reacts to good news.

questions.stem: How do you ask what the word こうばん means?
choices: 「こうばん」はどういういみですか。
questions.explanation: いみ is "meaning", so どういういみですか asks "what does it mean?". どこですか asks where a police box is, which is a different question.

questions.stem: You phone a friend's home. How do you ask to speak to Yui?
choices: もしもし、ゆいさんです。エマをおねがいします。
もしもし、ゆいさんはだれですか。
もしもし、エマです。ゆいさんをおねがいします。
しつれいします。ゆいさんがいります。
questions.explanation: Start with もしもし and your own name with です, then ask for the person with をおねがいします. The second answer swaps the names, だれ asks "who", and いります means "need".

questions.stem: What is the usual polite way to end a phone call?
questions.explanation: しつれいします closes a polite call (and is said when leaving a room). もしもし starts a call; いただきます is said before eating and おかえりなさい to someone coming home.

questions.stem: On the phone you hear 「{父|ちち}は{今|いま}るすです。」 What does it mean?
choices: My father is out at the moment.
My father is busy at the moment.
My father is on another call.
questions.explanation: るす means "being out, not at home". Busy would be いそがしい, and asleep ねています.

questions.stem: A friend says 「かぜをひいて、きのうはずっとねていました。」 Which reaction fits?
questions.explanation: Your friend was ill, so show sympathy: たいへんでしたね, "that must have been hard". よかったですね (I'm glad) and すごいですね (amazing) would sound as if being ill were good news, and なるほど means you've understood an explanation.

questions.stem: A friend says 「しけんはやさしかったです。」 Which reaction fits?
questions.explanation: Good news gets よかったですね, "I'm glad, that's great". たいへんですね is for problems.

questions.stem: Listen. What is happening?

audio.text: もしもし、エマです。

choices: Emma is ending a phone call.
Emma is starting a phone call.
questions.explanation: もしもし、エマです is how a phone call starts: "Hello, it's Emma." A call ends with しつれいします.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker want?

audio.text: すみません、もう少しゆっくりおねがいします。

choices: The other person to speak more slowly
The other person to repeat it once
questions.explanation: もう{少|すこ}しゆっくりおねがいします is "a little more slowly, please". "Once more" would be もういちど.

questions.stem: Listen. How does the speaker feel?

audio.text: へえ、すごいですね。

questions.explanation: へえ shows surprised interest and すごいですね admiration: "Wow, that's amazing." Sympathy would be たいへんですね.

questions.stem: Listen. When is the party?

audio.text: パーティーは四日ですか。いいえ、八日です。

questions.explanation: The first speaker asks about the 4th (よっか), but the answer corrects it: いいえ、{八日|ようか}です. After いいえ comes the real information.

questions.stem: Listen. Where is Tanaka?

audio.text: たなかは今、出かけています。

questions.explanation: {出|で}かけています is the ています form of {出|で}かける: he has gone out and is still out.

questions.stem: Listen. What will the speaker do?

audio.text: じゃあ、また後で電話します。

questions.explanation: また{後|あと}で{電話|でんわ}します is "I'll call again later". {電話|でんわ}します is the speaker's own action, not a request.

questions.stem: Listen and type what you hear, in hiragana: ___

audio.text: そうですか。

questions.explanation: そうですか, "I see; is that so?", the aizuchi for new information.

questions.stem: Listen and type the word you hear, in hiragana: ___

audio.text: もしもし

questions.explanation: もしもし is "hello" on the phone.

questions.stem: Match each aizuchi to when you use it.
questions.explanation: へえ for surprise, なるほど when you understand, たいへんですね for problems, よかったですね for good news. None of them is for saying goodbye: that's しつれいします or じゃあ、また.

questions.stem: How is 会話 read in "{日本語|にほんご}の会話はたのしいです。"?
questions.explanation: 会話 is かいわ, "conversation": the on'yomi カイ (as in {会社|かいしゃ}) and ワ (as in {電話|でんわ}). あ and はなし are kun'yomi used when the kanji stand alone ({会|あ}う, {話|はなし}).

questions.stem: How many levels does the JLPT have, and which is the easiest?
questions.explanation: The JLPT has five levels, N1 to N5. N5 is the first and easiest; N1 is the hardest.

questions.stem: Which skills does the JLPT test?
questions.explanation: The JLPT tests language knowledge, reading and listening, all with multiple-choice questions. There is no speaking test and no writing task.

questions.stem: What is the overall pass mark for N5?
questions.explanation: The N5 total runs from 0 to 180 and the overall pass mark is 80. You also need the minimum in each scoring section.

questions.stem: A candidate scores 105 in total: 90 in language knowledge and reading, 15 in listening. What is the result?
choices: Fail: listening is below its pass mark of 19.
Pass: listening isn't scored separately at N5.
Fail: the total must be at least 120.
questions.explanation: You must reach the overall pass mark (80) and each sectional pass mark: 38 of 120 for language knowledge and reading, 19 of 60 for listening. 15 in listening fails, whatever the total.

questions.stem: How is 来年 read in "来年しけんをうけます。"?
questions.explanation: 来年 is らいねん, "next year": on'yomi ライ + ネン. くる and とし are kun'yomi used when the kanji stand alone.

questions.stem: How long is the listening part of the N5 test?
questions.explanation: Listening takes 30 minutes. Vocabulary takes 20 minutes and grammar and reading 40.

questions.stem: In the JLPT listening part, how many times is each recording played?
questions.explanation: Each recording is played once, so read the choices first and let a missed item go.

questions.stem: 「だれがケーキを{食|た}べましたか。」「たなかさん___ケーキを{食|た}べました。」 Choose the particle.
questions.explanation: The answer to a question with だれが keeps が: the person is the new information. は would make たなかさん a topic, as if contrasting him with others, and を and で don't mark the subject.

questions.stem: {駅|えき}___コーヒーを{飲|の}みました。 Choose the particle (I had a coffee at the station).
questions.explanation: で marks the place where an action happens. に marks where something is or where you go, を the route, and へ a direction.

questions.stem: What is the て form of かえる (to go home)?
questions.explanation: かえる looks like a group 2 verb but is group 1, so る becomes って: かえって. かえて is the trap.

questions.stem: What is the past of いい (good)?
questions.explanation: いい uses the stem よ in its other forms: よかった (polite よかったです). いかった doesn't exist, and い-adjectives never take でした or だった for the past.

questions.stem: {日本|にほん}へ___ことがあります。 Choose the form (I have been to Japan).
questions.explanation: Experience is the た form + ことがあります: {行|い}ったことがあります. The dictionary form + ことがあります means "sometimes … happens", which is a different pattern.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "Please don't take photos here."?
choices: ここでしゃしんをとってください。
ここでしゃしんをとりませんでください。
ここでしゃしんをとらないでください。
ここでしゃしんをとるないでください。
questions.explanation: A request not to do something is the ない form + でください: とらないでください. ません can't go before でください, and とるない isn't a form.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "The room became clean."?
choices: へやがきれくなりました。
